issues.legal_issue: A judgment concerning a property right in an earlier proceeding is admissible as evidence of the assertion and recognition of that right even when the current litigant was not a party to the earlier proceeding.
material_facts: An earlier suit had resulted in a judgment declaring the institution’s title to the disputed land.
The plaintiff in the present suit was not a party to the earlier suit.
The institution relied on the earlier judgment as evidence of its title in the present property dispute.
issues.conclusion: The earlier judgment was admissible under Section 13 of the Evidence Act and could be relied on as evidence of the institution’s title, notwithstanding that the present plaintiff was not a party to it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 13 of the Evidence Act, a judgment not inter partes may be admitted as evidence of an assertion or recognition of a right to property. The Court relied on Srinivas Krishna Rao Kango v. Narayan Devji Kango, Sital Das v. Sant Ram, Dinamoni v. Brajmohini, and Collector of Gorakhpur v. Ram Sunder.

predicates.property_rights_dispute: The parties are litigating a right to property.
predicates.earlier_judgment_concerns_property_right: A judgment in an earlier proceeding addressed an asserted or recognized right to the property in dispute.
predicates.current_litigant_was_not_party_to_earlie: A litigant in the current dispute was not a party to the earlier proceeding.

issues.definition: When a property dispute involves an earlier judgment addressing a property right, that judgment may be admitted as evidence of the assertion or recognition of the right even if a current litigant was not a party to the earlier case.

issues.legal_issue: A court hearing a second appeal cannot reappreciate evidence accepted by the courts below on a factual issue such as possession.
material_facts: The trial court and the first appellate court assessed oral and documentary evidence concerning possession and accepted the evidence supporting the institution’s possession.
The second appellate court rejected evidence accepted by both lower courts and reassessed the parties’ evidence.
issues.conclusion: The second appellate court was not entitled to reappreciate the evidence and reject the factual findings on possession made by the courts below.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure limits a second appeal; the second appellate court cannot reappreciate evidence and displace factual findings made by the courts below on possession.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal.
predicates.lower_courts_accepted_evidence_on_factua: The courts below assessed evidence and accepted it in making a finding on a factual issue.
predicates.second_appellate_court_reassesses_that_e: The court hearing the second appeal reexamines that evidence and rejects the lower courts’ assessment.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, where the courts below accepted evidence on a factual issue, reassessment of that evidence by the second appellate court cannot displace their factual finding.

issues.legal_issue: A second appellate court cannot find that a party’s property title was extinguished by adverse possession when that issue was not raised in the courts below.
material_facts: The courts below found that the plaintiff had not proved the claimed long-term possession and that he had trespassed onto the land in 1967.
No issue of adverse possession had been raised in the courts below.
The second appellate court concluded for the first time that the institution’s title had been extinguished by adverse possession.
The evidence accepted by the courts below supported the institution’s possession after it obtained delivery of the land and until the plaintiff’s trespass.
issues.conclusion: The second appellate court’s finding that the institution’s title was extinguished was unsupportable and was set aside; the institution’s title had not been extinguished.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a second appellate court cannot make a new factual determination by deciding an issue that was not raised in the courts below. The finding of adverse possession also lacked support in the possession findings accepted by those courts.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal.
predicates.adverse_possession_issue_not_raised_belo: The parties did not raise adverse possession as an issue in the courts below.
predicates.second_appellate_court_finds_title_extin: The court hearing the second appeal finds that a party’s title was extinguished through another party’s adverse possession.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, a finding extinguishing title by adverse possession cannot stand when adverse possession was not raised as an issue in the courts below.

issues.legal_issue: A person suing for possession on the basis of prior possession after the summary remedy period has expired cannot recover possession from a defendant who proves a subsisting title to the property.
material_facts: The plaintiff was dispossessed while a temporary injunction was in force and later sought to amend the suit to claim possession after the summary remedy period had expired.
The suit was therefore considered as a regular suit based on possessory title.
The institution proved that it had title to the land and that its title had not been extinguished.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff could not recover possession on the basis of prior possession because the institution proved its subsisting title and was entitled to retain possession.
issues.legal_principle: Nair Service Society Ltd. v. K.C. Alexander holds that, after the time for a summary possession suit has expired, a dispossessed plaintiff may still sue on prior possession, but the defendant may establish title and remain in possession if that title is proved. The Court also relied on Sections 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, Articles 64 and 65 of the Limitation Act, Asher v. Whitlock, and Perry v. Clissold.

predicates.regular_possession_suit_based_on_prior_p: The proceeding is a regular suit seeking possession on the basis of the plaintiff’s prior possession.
predicates.plaintiff_was_dispossessed: The plaintiff had possession and was later put out of possession by another person.
predicates.summary_possession_remedy_period_expired: The plaintiff sought possession after the period for the summary remedy had expired.
predicates.defendant_proves_subsisting_property_tit: The defendant establishes a valid title to the property that remains in force.

issues.definition: A defendant who proves a subsisting property title may retain possession against a plaintiff relying on prior possession when the plaintiff’s summary possession remedy has expired.
